A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Gradient Aligned Regression via Pairwise Losses. All main-text and appendix material is readable and can be matched across the reformatting, with no material gaps preventing comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original synthetic and real-world regression experiments, runtime measurements, ablations, and sensitivity analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix B, including benchmark scores, runtime measurements, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The MAE component, two pairwise losses, KL-based aggregation, numerical stabilization, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The expanded expression in Equation 4 restates the existing loss, and the stochastic corollary does not introduce a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same two synthetic datasets and eight real-world tasks/settings across six benchmark datasets. The new stochastic corollary introduces no empirical noisy-data scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the synthetic experiments, real-world comparisons, and appendix studies, including PySR. The newly discussed RankNet, metric-learning, and AUROC methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The splits, models, metrics, training budgets, tuning grids, and evaluation procedures are retained. Synthetic settings formerly documented in v4 Appendix B.3 move into v5 Section 4.1 without changing their values.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the loss-component ablations, network-depth study, PySR search-space comparison, alpha and batch-size sensitivity analyses, moment-estimation curves, and standardization comparison. Renumbering and relocation introduce no new analysis.

E5.justification: Five-trial synthetic and AgeDB reporting, synthetic seeds, tabular cross-validation information, standard deviations, and Student's t-tests are unchanged. Moving the synthetic run information into the main text is not a new disclosure.

E6.justification: All seven tables match numerically, and Figures 1–12 retain identical plot content. For example, GAR's AgeDB MAE remains 6.286 for training from scratch and 6.069 for the RNC linear probe; the appendix ablation and sensitivity results also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds Corollary 5 and a proof sketch extending gradient matching to expected gradients for Y(x,z)=m(x)+z·s(x) with zero-mean noise. This is a limited extension obtained by applying Theorem 4 to m(x). The existing Appendix A proofs are unchanged, with the aggregation theorem renumbered from 5 to 6.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about label-space pairwise losses, gradient alignment, linear computational complexity, and empirical effectiveness. The stated clean-data scope is retained.

C2.justification: v5 explains how the gradient interpretation extends in expectation to zero-mean heteroskedastic stochastic targets. The introduction also expands the information-loss rationale for converting label similarities into ranks or positive/negative pairs. Section 5 retains the existing limitations concerning noise, outliers, and distribution shifts.

D1.justification: Implementation information, hyperparameters, IC50 preprocessing, hardware disclosure, and code-access information are retained. The fuller synthetic-settings paragraph in v5 Section 4.1 reproduces information already available in v4 Appendix B.3.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a paragraph on pairwise losses in other applications, citing Burges et al. (2005), Hadsell et al. (2006), and Gao and Zhou (2015). It distinguishes GAR through continuous labels, linear complexity, and independence from predefined similarity pairs, while retaining the existing regression positioning.

P1.justification: v5 makes localized language edits and expands explanations, moves synthetic settings into Section 4.1, places references before the appendices, and adds a generic Impact Statement. The main narrative and section hierarchy remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The single-column journal presentation becomes a two-column conference main text, with extensive changes to typography, headers, display sizing, and placement. Figures and tables are redistributed throughout the document, including Figure 12 moving to the final appendix page. The underlying plots and table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves theoretical context through the qualified stochastic extension and strengthens research positioning through the added cross-application discussion. These gains are limited: the experiments, results, and original proofs remain unchanged, and the stochastic extension does not resolve the stated empirical clean-data limitation. The extensive reformatting retains all evidence, although some appendix displays are farther from their discussion.
